findings.impact: Full account takeover of any user who views the poisoned ticket, including superadmins.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Authenticate as any ticket participant. 2) Post message containing . 3) Victim opens ticket detail or receives live WS update. 4) Script runs in victim session; steal session cookie / CSRF token / perform admin actions.
findings.recommendation: Remove |safe from message.message; use escape or bleach allowlist. In chat.js line ~442 wrap payload.message with escapeHtml(). Prefer textContent for message bodies.
findings.description: User chat messages rendered with Django |safe and chat.js innerHTML without escapeHtml on confirmed payloads.
findings.title: Stored XSS in ticket chat via |safe and unescaped WebSocket HTML

findings.impact: Complete compromise of the helpdesk on first deploy if defaults unchanged.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Deploy app and run migrate without changing DEFAULT_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD. 2) Attacker hits /accounts/login/ with admin/admin. 3) Full superuser access to tickets, users, SMTP settings, maintenance exports.
findings.playbook: 1) Revoke/disable default admin if exposed. 2) Rotate password to strong unique value. 3) Audit auth logs for admin logins. 4) Set env DEFAULT_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD before any new deploy. 5) Do not rely on git history scrub for this (password is in code defaults, not a leaked live key).
findings.recommendation: Fail migrate if DEFAULT_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD is missing/weak in non-DEBUG. Force requires_password_change=True. Rotate any deployed default credentials immediately.
findings.description: post_migrate creates superuser from DEFAULT_SUPERADMIN_* defaults (admin/admin) documented in README and .env.example.
findings.title: Default superadmin created with admin/admin on migrate

findings.impact: Cross-department ticket takeover and data exposure.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Login as support in Dept Y with can_pick_ticket. 2) Obtain ticket ID from another department (sequential IDs or enumeration). 3) POST /tickets/<id>/pick/. 4) Ticket assigned to attacker; PII and chat accessible.
findings.recommendation: Require ticket.department_id == user.department_id (or branch scope for branch users) before pick, matching TicketListView filters.
findings.description: Any user with can_pick_ticket can assign themselves any unassigned ticket regardless of department.
findings.title: pick_ticket missing department/branch scope check

findings.impact: Cross-tenant ticket hijack and confidential history access.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Login as any support agent. 2) POST status change on closed ticket in another department to in_progress. 3) Ticket reopens and assigns to attacker.
findings.recommendation: Enforce department/branch ownership on closed-ticket updates; restrict reopen to assignee, same-dept leads, or explicit can_update_closed_ticket with scope.
findings.description: Closed-ticket branch of update_ticket_status allows any user_type==support with no department check; reopen sets assigned_to=request.user.
findings.title: Any support user can reopen any closed ticket and self-assign

findings.impact: Stored XSS / malware distribution via trusted media URLs.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Authenticated user uploads xss.html or xss.svg as ticket attachment. 2) Victim opens /media/tickets/<id>/xss.html. 3) Browser executes script on app origin.
findings.recommendation: Validate extension+size in TicketMessage.clean and forms; store under UUID filenames; serve with Content-Disposition: attachment and auth-gated media view in all environments.
findings.description: MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE and ALLOWED_ATTACHMENT_EXTENSIONS unused. FileField accepts any type. DEBUG serves /media/ without auth.
findings.title: Attachment allowlist/size never enforced; uploadable HTML/SVG XSS

findings.impact: Horizontal privilege escalation / cross-branch PII leak.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Ticket in Branch A linked to published KB article. 2) User from Branch B opens /tickets/<id>/. 3) Access granted; client phone, description, message history visible.
findings.recommendation: Remove has_kb_access from ticket authorization; link KB from ticket UI only for users who already pass branch/dept checks, or show a redacted KB-only card.
findings.description: has_kb_access OR bypasses branch/department checks on TicketDetailView and TicketDrawerPartialView, exposing full ticket including messages.
findings.title: Published KB article grants cross-branch/department ticket view

findings.impact: Session forgery, information disclosure, cache poisoning via Host header.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Deploy with incomplete .env. 2) DEBUG leaks traces; ALLOWED_HOSTS=* enables Host-header attacks; predictable SECRET_KEY enables session forgery.
findings.recommendation: Require SECRET_KEY from env with no weak default when DEBUG is false; default DEBUG=0; refuse to start if ALLOWED_HOSTS is * outside DEBUG.
findings.description: SECRET_KEY, DEBUG, and ALLOWED_HOSTS default to unsafe values suitable only for local demo; README documents same.
findings.title: Insecure production defaults: DEBUG=1, ALLOWED_HOSTS=*, weak SECRET_KEY default

findings.impact: Mailbox takeover / outbound phishing as the helpdesk.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker with email settings access or XSS steals SMTP password from DB/HTML. 2) Abuse org mailbox for phishing.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt at rest (Fernet/KMS); never render_value; mask in UI; rotate SMTP app passwords after fix.
findings.description: EmailSetting.smtp_password is plain CharField; PasswordInput(render_value=True) embeds secret in HTML for email managers.
findings.title: SMTP passwords stored and re-rendered in plaintext

findings.exploit_scenario: 1) If cookies are sent cross-site (legacy browser / SameSite=None misconfig), evil page opens wss://helpdesk/... as victim. 2) Read notifications/chat or send messages.
findings.recommendation: Wrap with AllowedHostsOriginValidator(AuthMiddlewareStack(...)); tighten ALLOWED_HOSTS; consider Origin allowlist.
findings.description: AuthMiddlewareStack alone; Channels docs recommend AllowedHostsOriginValidator. SameSite=Lax reduces classic CSWSH but control is still missing; ALLOWED_HOSTS=* weakens validator if added alone.
findings.title: WebSocket stack missing AllowedHostsOriginValidator
